detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure: PagerDuty REST include[]=subscribers or custom workflow enrichment.
• Data: PagerDuty incidents with stakeholder subscriber lists (`subscriber_emails` MV field).
• For directory layout and inputs, see docs/implementation-guide.md.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Truncate emails at ingest for privacy; use hashed IDs in shared indexes.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following search (then save as report or alert; tune time range and threshold):

```spl
index=alerts sourcetype="pagerduty:incident"
| where urgency="high" OR severity="critical"
| eval sub_count=mvcount(subscriber_emails)
| where sub_count>25
| stats avg(sub_count) as avg_sub by service_name
| sort -avg_sub
```

Understanding this search
Over-subscribed SEV-1 incidents flood executives and slow consensus.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with the PagerDuty incident timeline and service view for the same window. Reconcile a few incident numbers, state changes, and acknowledgement times. If anything disagrees, check export lag, time zone, and which API fields we map.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add to a dashboard, wire alert actions, and document ownership. Suggested view: Bar chart (avg subscribers), Table (service).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (PagerDuty REST include[]=subscribers or custom workflow enrichment — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=pagerduty:incident into alerts. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`service_name, sub_count`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
